title: Add exporter metrics (lag/retries/throughput), basic tracing, and structured logs
author: Caleb Johnson
body: Summary: This PR adds first-pass Prometheus metrics + basic tracing + structured logging to the audit-log-exporter service. Metrics are aligned to Redwood observability naming/cardinality standards (per Allison/Logan feedback) and provide the signals needed for initial dashboards/alerts (lag, throughput, retries, adapter errors). This work is scoped to exporter-side instrumentation only; the control plane status endpoint will consume these signals via existing health paths and the observability pack dashboards will be done separately. Context: ENG-5168. Motivation: During beta soak we’ve been debugging exporter lag spikes and downstream 429/backpressure mostly via ad-hoc logs. We need stable metrics to (a) quantify export lag vs SLO, (b) separate downstream throttling from internal queueing, (c) support paging policy (page on sustained lag / hard failures, ticket on transient retries), and (d) give Support/CS a consistent way to answer “are we exporting?” Implementation details (metrics): Adds a dedicated Prometheus registry for the service and standardizes metric names under the audit exporter namespace. Key metrics: 1) redwood_audit_exporter_export_lag_seconds (gauge): computed as now() - last_successful_checkpoint_timestamp, exported per destination_type and tenant_tier only (no tenant_id/export_config_id labels). 2) redwood_audit_exporter_events_exported_total (counter): increments per event successfully handed off to an adapter (post-filtering), labels: destination_type, result=success|retryable_error|fatal_error. 3) redwood_audit_exporter_batches_exported_total (counter): increments per batch attempt, labels: destination_type, result=success|retryable_error|fatal_error, http_status_class=2xx|4xx|5xx|none (where applicable). 4) redwood_audit_exporter_batch_send_duration_seconds (histogram): adapter send latency, labels: destination_type, result; buckets tuned to cover typical HEC/Datadog/S3 behavior (including a long tail for throttling scenarios). 5) redwood_audit_exporter_retries_total (counter) and redwood_audit_exporter_retry_backoff_seconds (histogram): records retry loop activity and backoff durations. 6) redwood_audit_exporter_dlq_batches_total (counter) and redwood_audit_exporter_dlq_depth (gauge): DLQ health signals. 7) redwood_audit_exporter_config_sync_success_total / _failure_total (counters) and redwood_audit_exporter_config_sync_age_seconds (gauge): config sync observability. Notes on naming/cardinality: Per observability standards, labels avoid high-cardinality identifiers (tenant UUID, export_config_id, destination host). Those identifiers are emitted in structured logs only. destination_type is one of: splunk_hec|datadog_logs|s3. tenant_tier is derived from config (hosted|dedicated) for now; private is not expected in beta. Implementation details (tracing): Adds OpenTelemetry spans around the exporter batch lifecycle (fetch -> filter -> adapt/send -> checkpoint). Span names follow Redwood conventions: audit_exporter.fetch, audit_exporter.filter, audit_exporter.adapter.send, audit_exporter.checkpoint.write. Attributes include destination_type, batch_size_events, and retry_attempt (bounded). Trace context is propagated through internal goroutines; adapter HTTP clients now attach trace headers where applicable. Tracing is intentionally lightweight (no per-event spans) to avoid overhead and cardinality explosions. Implementation details (structured logs): Switches exporter logs to a consistent JSON structure with stable keys: service=audit-log-exporter, component=exporter|adapter|checkpoint|config_sync, destination_type, export_stream=primary, attempt, batch_id (opaque UUID), and error_kind (classification for retry/backoff policies). tenant_id/workspace_id are included only at INFO for control-plane initiated operations and at DEBUG for hot paths; by default we log export_config_id only when errors occur (to help CS/SRE triage) and we explicitly do not log payload/event bodies. Also adds log redaction safeguards for credential fields (ensures tokens/keys never render via fmt/%+v). Testing: - Unit tests for metric label validation and histogram bucket sanity. - Updated adapter tests to assert that errors are classified consistently (retryable vs fatal) and emit the right counters. - Manual: ran local harness with Splunk/Datadog stubs and confirmed metrics scrape at /metrics, spans in local collector, and logs include trace_id/span_id. Ops/rollout: Metrics are behind the existing service config flag observability.metrics_enabled (default true in staging, false in local unless explicitly enabled). Tracing is gated by OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT presence; if not set, spans are no-op. No changes to request processing semantics. Follow-ups: - Add dashboards/alerts in observability-pack (separate PR). - Revisit export_lag_seconds definition when we add per-destination checkpoint streams (currently one checkpoint per destination config). - Confirm alert thresholds with SRE once we have beta traffic baselines. Changelog/notes: No API changes. No customer-facing behavior change beyond improved operational visibility.
commits: wire prometheus registry + /metrics handler for exporter service
instrument exporter pipeline: lag gauge, throughput counters, duration histograms
add OTel spans around fetch/filter/send/checkpoint; plumb context through adapters
convert exporter logs to structured JSON + add redaction guards
tests: label cardinality guardrails + adapter error classification assertions
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Please avoid tenant_id/export_config_id labels; we’ve had incidents with cardinality blow-ups. destination_type + tenant_tier is fine. Also: can we align histogram buckets with our defaults (0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 30, 60)?

Caleb Johnson (author): Agreed. Removed tenant_id/export_config_id labels and moved those fields to structured logs. Updated send duration buckets to match standards and added a longer tail bucket (120s) for downstream throttling scenarios.

Logan Wright: Lag metric definition: is it last successful checkpoint time or last attempted? For SLO we care about successful delivery. Also, please make sure gauge is monotonic-increasing during outage (shouldn’t reset due to retries).
Caleb Johnson (author): Lag is based on last successful checkpoint write. It only resets on success. During downstream outage it will increase with wall time; retries do not change it.

Sean Gallagher: For paging we’ll likely alert on sustained lag + sustained failures. Can we add a per-destination “last_success_age_seconds” gauge as well? It’s easier to reason about than lag when clocks drift.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added redwood_audit_exporter_last_success_age_seconds as an alias gauge computed the same way (now - last_success_ts). We can pick whichever reads better in dashboards.
Aisha Bello: Please ensure /metrics endpoint is protected by the same internal auth as /health (or at least not exposed publicly). What’s the exposure in hosted?

Caleb Johnson (author): /metrics is served on the internal admin port only (same listener as /healthz). In k8s, it’s behind cluster network policy; no external ingress. Added a note to docs/ops/metrics.md.
Allison Grant: Structured logs: confirm we never log headers/tokens. I saw a %+v on adapter config in one place.
Caleb Johnson (author): Fixed: removed %+v on destination config; added explicit redaction wrappers and a unit test that fails if known secret keys appear in log output.
Logan Wright: Looks good. Approving once CI is green.
release_notes: Internal: audit-log-exporter now emits Prometheus metrics for export lag/retries/throughput and includes basic tracing + structured logs for better on-call triage.
